utterances.text: Now if there's a civilian user who is calling from abroad, where would the call have to travel, along what route for it to have been captured -- to have been intercepted before reaching Crna Rijeka? So what I'm interested in is the route of a communication -- of a telephone call that was put in by someone who's calling from abroad, a civilian caller. So let's start. The caller is on a -- on a civilian line and it would arrive, I take it, at either the Sokolac PTT or the -- the Pale PTT and then travel along the route you've described. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it depends if a Sokolac number was called from the post of Sokolac to Crna Rijeka. If from Pale, then the Pale route, if it is a Pale PTT number.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And in both instances, it's anyway passing through Strazbenica to Veliki Zep; right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So I'd like to look at another intercept now, and this is 65 ter 21062b, and this is an under seal intercept, and it's just an example I'd like you to take a look at. It's a communication intercepted by the State Security Service, the Bosnian State Security Service, from the 17th of July, 1995. And you will see in the header there: "On that day, while monitoring the Pale axis on frequency 836.000 megahertz, channel 13, at 2340 hours, we recorded a conversation between General Ratko Mladic and Milos Kostic, whom we did not hear." Now, do you know at all what users were using channel 13 on that frequency?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any of this. I don't know Mr. Kostic. I don't know this channel 13. I really don't know which radio route this is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: All right. Do you -- now, here we only hear one side of the conversation, and Milos Kostic is not heard at all. Are you familiar with somebody by that name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That question has been answered already, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "I don't know Mr. Kostic."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now it's our position, Witness, that on the 17th of July, and there's evidence in this case, that General Mladic is in Crna Rijeka, and it's our position that he's speaking to Milos Kostic, who we believe to be in the United States. So isn't this an example of what we've been talking about, which is that Milos Kostic is calling from the United States using clearly a civilian line, and that his call comes in either to Sokolac PTT centre or Pale PTT centre, and he gets transferred along the path that you've described to reach Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said this is possible, but I'm telling you again I don't know Kostic and I don't know which route was taken because I don't know the number that the man used to call. I mean, there were different numbers from different centres, so I cannot say now. It went along such and such a route, this conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, the witness is apparently not in a position to say anything about it because you present the facts, whereas we always expect the witness to present facts here, if this and if that, if that is then, so the witness says he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just trying to put our case to the witness. Now, the fact that he doesn't know this particular communication is not -- is not exactly what I'm getting at. I'm just trying to establish along what routes must this call have gone through, and I think he's already described the routes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He has described the routes. You're telling that he's calling from aboard. The witness doesn't know, so the witness is not in a position to confirm anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And that's why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you could, of course, later argue that if there's evidence that this person calls from abroad that it fits well in the description given by this witness. But that's argument rather than testimony of a witness of fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: -- I'm just trying to get and I am putting a hypothetical question to him: If he accepts the fact that someone is calling from the United States, and I understand that that's a fact I'm putting to him, along what path would that communication travel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Pajic, for this communication to have been intercepted, and we see here it says on the Pale axis, and you've described to us the route from Pale, that communication would have travelled along the route you've already described to us to reach Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, in order to be able to confirm something I have to know. I have to know from which number -- or rather which PTT number was used by someone to call General Mladic. In this case, it was General Mladic's Belgrade number. There was also a Han Pijesak number. Then there was a number at the switchboard, the Sokolac PTT number. Now, they all take different routes, and I cannot confirm that to you now; it took such and such a route and could be listened to on such and such a route. So he had a civilian PTT number that came from a completely different relay from Belgrade through Ser to Veliki Zep. The civilian PTT number from Han Pijesak took a wire communication to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, and the PTT Sokolac number that took the relay communication that I already described via --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you just slow down. I know the interpreters are -- it looks like they're keeping up, but I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask a simple question. Earlier a question was asked about the civilian user calling from aboard, and then you said: "Yes, it depends if a Sokolac number was called from the post of Sokolac to Crna Rijeka. If from Pale, then the Pale route, if it is a Pale PTT number." And you confirmed that it's passing through the Strazbenica and Veliki Zep, and you said, yes, that's how it happens. Would that be any different if the person would be calling from the United States?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course there's a difference. I repeat once again: General Mladic had several civilian PTT numbers that took different routes. So the civilian number in Belgrade that was called most often came from Avala Cer to Veliki Zep. Then the civilian number from Han Pijesak that took wire communication from Han Pijesak. I don't know which number this call is coming from, from abroad. So all of this was in Crna Rijeka but there were different routes that were taken if they were from different telephone exchanges, Sokolac, Pale, Belgrade, it doesn't matter. There was just Han Pijesak, Sokolac, and Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, we have -- the Prosecution has spoken to General Milovanovic, and we can call up 65 ter 32034 for the benefit of the Defence and the Chamber, and he said that if someone is calling from abroad, let's say, as the case that I just showed you, from the United States, and if that person wanted to speak to General Mladic in Belgrade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would finish your question, then Mr. Ivetic has an opportunity to object if he wishes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Then his call, the call that's put in from the United States, would have been connected to General Mladic in his apartment in Belgrade via the FRY headquarters in Belgrade. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The number given by my colleague is not anything related to Mr. Milovanovic, so I would ask for that to be clarified and then perhaps -- I don't know if what she called up is something that is identifiable or if we need a reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The number is 65 ter 32644.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then I would want on the record that we were not disclosed this statement from a witness of [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I will just wait for Ms. Stewart to provide us with a date on when this information report was disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can we meanwhile -- I take it we can continue the -- your question and your observation is on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Pajic, do you need me to repeat the question? Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Repeat it once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. So do you agree with what General Milovanovic told us, which is that if a caller was trying to reach General Mladic in his apartment in Belgrade, that that call would have been connected to General Mladic via the FRY headquarters in Belgrade? That's the route that that call would have taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please scroll down in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We can look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic is also on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think it might be the same thing. The question is now being asked differently than was originally stated, as the origination of the call.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The originator of the call, and I gave an example of the United States, is calling from the United States -- a civilian from the United States is trying to reach General Mladic in his apartment in Belgrade. What General Milovanovic told us is that call would have been connected to General Mladic via the FRY headquarters in Belgrade. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was calling General Mladic to Belgrade but that person had the number where General Mladic could be reached. Why would he call at Crna Rijeka? The PTT number coming from Belgrade went along the route Avala Ser --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I stop you. You may have not clearly understood the question. Ms. Hasan, I leave it in your hands. We are not specifically talking about this conversation any further but about what General Milovanovic told in an interview. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. So I think I have your answer which is what also General Milovanovic explained to us, which is that call would not have been connected via the RS territory through the radio relay network in the RS territory. If -- if -- if the civilian user is reaching Mladic in Belgrade, it's going directly to Belgrade, not through the RS to Belgrade. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And what General Milovanovic went on to tell us is that a civilian user calling from abroad who's trying to reach Mladic in Crna Rijeka when, in fact, Mladic is in Belgrade, that that person would not have been put through by an operator to Belgrade. Do you agree with that? And let me be clear: That an operator from Crna Rijeka would not have connected the civilian user to Belgrade to enable him to -- him or her to reach General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And that's because there were security implications for -- related to revealing General Mladic's whereabouts; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he was staying in Belgrade, he had some sort of PTT number where he could be reached at all times, and that's where people called him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So it would be incumbent on the civilian user who is trying to reach General Mladic to call directly Belgrade and reach him there?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He received information from the ADC of General Mladic in Crna Rijeka and then that person would dial General Mladic at the given number.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And who is the ADC?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Rajko Banduka.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So Captain Rajko Banduka would be the person who would then decide whether to reveal to the -- to the user who is calling that Mladic is in Belgrade? But he would tell him to call Belgrade, the Belgrade number, if at all.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's probably what General Mladic himself would tell him when he decided which call to accept, which not, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, if Mladic was in Belgrade, okay, and General Mladic is calling from a PTT line in Belgrade, and he's trying to reach the duty officer at Crna Rijeka, so not -- I'm not talking about Captain Rajko Banduka but the duty officer, can you tell us how that call would be connected?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a radio relay communications between the Main Staff of the VRS and the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. There was one protected and one unprotected. There was no problem for him to call anyone at the General Staff in Belgrade through the military switchboard in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we take a look at Exhibit P1655, and this is an under seal exhibit. And Ms. Stewart advises me that the information report was disclosed in disclosure batch 119, which was a DVD that was placed in the Defence's locker on Friday, the 15th of May, 2015.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So this is an intercept, and this shouldn't be broadcast. Again, it's a state security intercepted communication, and the communication date is 16 July 1995. And the header reads: "On the above date, monitoring the Pale radio relay on frequency 836.000 megahertz, channel 13, at 1615 hours, we recorded a conversation between the duty officer in the Main Staff and General Mladic, who was inaudible." So, again, this is another example where only one side of the communication -- one of the participants was heard. Now, the Defence and the Prosecution agree that, at this time, 1615 hours, General Mladic was in Belgrade. So this is General Mladic in Belgrade speaking to the Main Staff's duty officer, who sits in Crna Rijeka; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if General Mladic was in Belgrade and he was talking with the duty operations officer in Crna Rijeka or whoever, and this was intercepted at some section in Pale, it's impossible. Because there was a route directed from Veliki Zep through Cer towards Belgrade and you could hear only one side of the conversation. First of all, I'm not familiar with this conversation. Second, Pale has nothing to do with it nor the Pale radio relay route. It has nothing do with this conversation between Belgrade and the Main Staff. Let me repeat: This is the section Veliki Zep via Cer which is in Serbia, and Mount Avala, outside Belgrade. If this was intercepted and the intercepter claims that this was along the Pale radio relay route, that's nonsense. Where is the other side of the conversation? Where is the entire conversation so we can confirm some things?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We're not -- for this purpose, it's -- we're not interested in the entire conversation but we're just interested in -- in the routes here. So, now, if General Mladic is calling from a PTT line, let's say General Mladic is calling from his apartment or, for example, from the VMA, so he is using a civilian PTT line, can you tell us the routes that his call would travel? And can you start -- start at the beginning. So his PTT line would arrive where?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If General Mladic would use a PTT number in Belgrade where you claim he was would call Crna Rijeka on a PTT number, he had, in his own office with the ADC Banduka, a civilian PTT number. So from his PTT number in Belgrade, he could call the PTT number in his own office. This one, this route was Veliki Zep-Cer-Avala. Mladic had no need to call in any other direction. In Belgrade, he had only the PTT number. With other numbers, he could communicate using the manual, normal switchboard. Why would he call in Crna Rijeka a different civilian number when he had his own?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now if he's calling using that -- his own civilian number, that communication would not have been intercepted; right? I mean, theoretically the wirelines may have been intercepted but let's just keep it to the radio relay.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a radio relay connection. Let me repeat once more: Mladic had a civilian number in his office in Han Pijesak, and when he called that number from Belgrade, it would go from Veliki Zep to Avala. It's the system SMC-1306B. Although it's analogue, it's perfectly safe. You cannot -- you have to mount an incredible amount of equipment in order to listen into that, and I explained to you already how close the intercepter would have to be to both stations. In this situation, that was impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And the manual -- the normal switchboard you're talking about is located where?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That switchboard, I already explained when we were discussing the switch, that was room number 1 in the underground part of the installation. Room marked 1A.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. So if he's calling trying to reach the switchboard to then be connected to the duty officer in Crna Rijeka, his communication is travelling over the radio relay network; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, it has to go through a radio relay connection although it's in Belgrade, and he has several possibilities. He has the option to call from his apartment in Belgrade from his PTT number. He could call the PTT number which is in the switchboard in the exchange of the General Staff in Belgrade, and they could directly transfer him to my telephone exchange in Crna Rijeka. That connection still exists, although I don't believe it went that way. My telephone exchange - that is, the exchange of the Main Staff - had a direct protected connection with the exchange of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia in Belgrade. He could make telephone calls that way. And that's what he normally did. He usually -- I mean, he exclusively used secure lines when he was calling from Belgrade. Although it doesn't mean that he couldn't use the other option.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And in respect of the other option, you -- were there several possibilities for that communication travelling to Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, the communication system is a very large system. There are a number of options. He used mainly these two. He mainly used secure lines, and communications were operating, of course. There were connections with all the corps. The exchanges of the corps were connected to the Main Staff, of course, and they had both analogue and digital connections, each corps did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The connection that existed between Cer and Veliki Zep, okay, that segment, there was an SMC-1306B operating along that route; right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had two radio relay routes with Cer, that is, to Belgrade. One was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked again to slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, the interpreters asked that you slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I really forget myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer. You started off saying: "We had two radio relay routes with Cer, that is, to Belgrade. One was ..."

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't receive interpretation at this moment on the English channel. Could you restart your answer on from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Towards Cer, that is to say Belgrade, the communication was along two radio relay connections. One was a digital or protected one, and the number of that route was 0719. The second relay route also towards Cer and on towards Avala, Belgrade, was 1058. That was its number. And the device used was SMC-1306B. And the entire route was protected; that is to say, 0719, but towards Avala, the number was 7001.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: From Cer to Veliki Zep, there was a backup RRU-800 operating, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That device was in the process of preparation. It never worked. But in case of air strikes or the SMC device broke down, that device was planned to be activated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just going to review my notes to see how much more I need to go through.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So a communication travelling on that RRU-800 from Cer to Veliki Zep, we agree that that would have been an open line that could have been intercepted?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection. That misstates the evidence. The witness clearly said at line 7 it never worked, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I can rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That line -- should that RRU-800 have been operating from Cer to Veliki Zep, that would have been an open line that could have been intercepted; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, that would be the analogue unprotected route. But let me repeat once again. That was a backup piece of equipment. That device was never used. It was just there in -- if SMC broke down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no need to repeat that. Ms. Hasan was just inquiring to the kind of line it would have been if operational.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Could we take a look at P1655 and -- I'm sorry, P1658, please, and this is another under seal exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And this is, Mr. Pajic, an intercepted communication on the same date, on the 16th of July, and it's a communication between General Mladic and a Kostic, at 2250 hours. It's intercepted on the same frequency, 836.000 megahertz, on the Pale axis. Now, can we turn to page 2 in the English to see the relevant intercept. So the one we're interested in is -- you can see it there, number 672, the communication on the bottom half of this document. Now you previously told us that if a civilian was trying to reach General Mladic at Crna Rijeka and General Mladic was not present at Crna Rijeka but was present at Belgrade, that his call would not have travelled through the RS radio relay network but rather he would either have been not connected at all or he would have been given a number to reach General Mladic directly in Belgrade. So my question to you is that this communication which comes into a civilian telephone line and is intercepted on the radio relay network, necessarily meant that General Mladic was within the RS territory and not in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, I don't know where General Mladic was. You can't see it from this document. There is some kind of intercept, but I don't know at which number they were looking for him. It makes a big difference on which number he was called, if it was a civilian number. These people from aboard, let me repeat, called me at the civilian PTT number that was located with his ADC in Crna Rijeka, and 90 per cent of those communications went through his ADC. He almost never used the manual switchboard. Banduka can confirm that. All his conversations with UNPROFOR, with foreign countries, et cetera, went through his civilian PTT number in Belgrade. And that one enters the radio relay communications from Belgrade at Avala, that is, through Cer, to Veliki Zep.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I understand your answer and what you're saying. My question is a little bit the reverse of what your saying, which is: Kostic calling from the United States, and that's a fact I'm putting to you, I'm asking you to accept that Kostic is calling from abroad, his call is coming in and is being intercepted in the radio relay network of the RS. And what you had told us before is that a civilian calling, trying to reach General Mladic, would not have travelled -- would not have been -- sorry. He would not have been put through to General Mladic over the radio relay network but rather he would have either been told where General Mladic is, if that was the decision made, and told to directly contact him in Belgrade, therefore bypassing the radio relay network in the RS and making it impossible to intercept that call. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, if somebody is calling General Mladic at a civilian number in Belgrade instead of his civilian Belgrade number located in his office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you one question. Do I understand that -- what route it took to get through to General Mladic depended on what the caller would choose as the number he wished to reach, whether that was a Belgrade number or whether that was a number at Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if -- yes, that's not on the record. I heard you whispering "okay." Is that what I heard? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you understood that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you wanted to choose to reach him in Crna Rijeka, you would dial the number and that would be -- that would travel over the radio relay system. If you wished to call him in Belgrade, you would choose another number and that would not travel over the radio relay system in Republika Srpska. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's about five minutes to the break. If you would allow us to take the break early, I'll reassess what I have left and I may have a few questions left or none at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then before we do so, Mr. Ivetic, I don't know -- let's just assume that Ms. Hasan would need anything between five and ten minutes for a few questions or no questions at all, how much time would you need? And I'm asking this so that Mr. Stojanovic can consult with Mr. Mladic as to what he prefers to do at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're on the same page. That's what I thought. I have about 10 to 12 minutes right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that we most likely would start the testimony of the next witness still today. Yes. Then we take the break. Mr. Pajic, you heard that most likely you will be excused later on today. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. We'll resume at 25 minutes to 2.00, and I assure you that I will not have to make apologies again for a late start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, have you made up your mind? Should Mr. Ivetic already prepare or should he wait for another second?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'll just have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we take a look at 65 ter 05923b, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You'll see, Mr. Pajic, that this is the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska phonebook. It's dated August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we turn to page 2 in both the English and B/C/S, Your Honours, this is an excerpt from the complete phonebook.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We see the page which lists a number of phone numbers for the Main Staff, starting with other telephone -- automatic telephone exchanges connected to G-1 automatic telephone exchange. And it lists there a number -- phone numbers for various PTT centres, automatic telephone exchanges. And is my understanding correct: That 011 was the -- the number you had to call before dialing a Belgrade phone?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this number, 011 199 208, if you're calling a Belgrade number, you just directly dial the six-digit or seven-digit number in Belgrade. You don't need the city code 011.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So if you're calling Belgrade PTT automatic telephone exchange from the RS you would have to dial the complete number, right, including the code, 011?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've told you: If you call a civilian PTT number in Belgrade, you don't need to dial 011 from Crna Rijeka, if you're calling this first number on this list. From this number, you directly dial any other number in Belgrade. You don't need to use the city code, 011. I don't know if you're understanding that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one follow-up question. Wouldn't that depend on from where you call?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't matter. You can call from anywhere, if it's this number; Han Pijesak, Banja Luka, anywhere. If it that's number, then you don't have to dial 011. That is an existing Belgrade number that is installed there through relay channels. You are not going into a different network. You are dealing within the same network, the 011 network. The Belgrade network. I don't know if you understand what I'm saying now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're calling from the 011 network, you don't have to dial it. If you call from outside the 011 network, you would have to dial the full number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For example, if you are dialling this telephone -- if you're calling from this number in Crna Rijeka, if you're calling this other number, then you need to use the area code 071 and then the six-digit number. But if you're calling from that Belgrade network number another Belgrade network number, then you don't need the area code.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's standard for all countries, I think. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And Crna Rijeka was in the 011 network? Was Crna Rijeka in the same network as 011?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Crna Rijeka was not in that network. It was only that Belgrade number that was in Crna Rijeka that was. 011 199 208. That number belonged to the Belgrade network.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand now.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we see just below that the numbers that one would have to dial to reach the PTT centre in Sokolac?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you don't have to dial anything. You take the receiver and you call 868-042, you hear the signal from the Sokolac PTT. You can dial any number in Sokolac. You can do that for Han Pijesak and Pale. For all these numbers where the area code is 071, you don't have to do anything. You just lift the receiver. So that number was at the switchboard in Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: All right. I think we're in agreement on that. Now you see below it says: Other automatic telephone exchanges connected to the operations centre, and we see military automatic telephone exchange with G-1. And there's an extension there, 153. You recall that extension?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see where it says military ATC from G-1, 153, you lift the receiver and you dial another three-digit number. It depends where because they were practically at all the switchboards of all the corps, so you can choose any number that is at the hand-held switchboard at G-1. You can dial any number outside Crna Rijeka that was connected to other corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was whether you remember that number, 153.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this is in the operations centre. In the operations centre -- well, I've forgotten the exact number already, but that is what is written here. Operations centre is the duty officer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please focus your answer very much on the questions. We'd like to have you excused till today and by focusing your answer on the questions, that would help. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If I was calling from the Drina Corps switchboard, for example, and I wanted to reach the military automatic telephone exchange at G-1, what number would I dial?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether you registered it yesterday, the three-digit ATC was 332 at the exchange in the Drina Corps, and it went along a protected channel. I don't know if you noticed that. I explained that yesterday and I said which channels were protected. So 332, number 332 for the same switchboard was for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is the number you'd have to dial? Don't tell us about what connections protected or not. What number would you have to dial from the -- the Drina Corps switchboard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you want to reach 153, if you want the telephone switchboard three 2s or 9. I don't know what they want. I don't know what they're selecting. So operations centre 153, the telephone exchange, 222 or 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we turn the page in both the English and -- well, in the English first.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we now see under the heading "Commander," military automatic telephone exchange with G-1, 161. And so that I understand correctly, I mean, this is a phone book, so if I want to reach the commander of the Main Staff, am I to dial one of these numbers that's listed here?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends which number you're calling from. If it's the three digit switchboard, then you call this first number, if you're calling from the G-1 switchboard.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Right. So -- and we see that in order to reach General Mladic, we see that he's got a protected -- one protected military line which is a -- a Belgrade military -- from the Belgrade military automatic telephone exchange, as well as from Belgrade he's got a protected civilian PTT line and the numbers are provided there. Does that accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian PTT line.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot follow at this speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you slow down and start your answer again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is written here is Belgrade ATC, 22-984. That was a military five-digit number in Belgrade. It is a number that General Mladic had in Crna Rijeka in his office there. It's a protected number.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And that's -- we see it says protected there under Belgrade PTT, so that's -- that's also a protected line; right? And that's what you remember, there was --

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see a translation here on the right-hand side, and over here I cannot see it on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, it may be that we have to move to the next page -- no, we are on the right page. One second. Yes. Could you look at the -- the -- the -- where it says "commander" and then the following four lines. You see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you also see the Belgrade PTT - protected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And so these two -- these two lines are designated protected. Now, the military automatic telephone exchange with G-1, you would -- we're not talking here about a protected line, so to speak; right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it cannot be a protected line since it was from General Mladic's office to the switchboard 20 metres from Vila Javor to the underground office. That was 20 or 30 metres of cable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then, Witness, it is an internal line and therefore needs no protection. Is that what you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just want to explain this here. It says here protected, for both numbers, because they come along this route from Belgrade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I was focusing on the military ATC with G-1, 161. That's an internal line. It's just another connection internally and therefore needs no protection. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Internal line, yes, if General Mladic is not using it. However, as he is dialling some other number from that number, that is, within the Drina Corps, then he has to use a protected line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Next question, please, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you then explain the fourth number down there, Pale PTT automatic telephone exchange, 071 783-371 [sic]. Sorry, I'll repeat that: 071 783-375. Could you explain how that connected to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why it's not written here. It also went through 0601 to Pale. It was also a protected line. This is a Pale number, 783-375. It took the protected route: Veliki Zep-Ravna Romanija-Kalovita Brda and down there to Pale and then we brought this number that way to Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you previously told us that that route was also unprotected?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that route. I said that this one was protected, 0601 -- no, sorry, 0661. Sorry. That was protected. Whereas, this is the analogue one that I was speaking about that goes through Strazbenica-Jahorina to Pale, and specifically this number, 06 -- no, 783-375, it took 0661. This is a protected route: Veliki Zep-Ravno Romanija-Kalovita Brda-Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you have no explanation why that's not designated protected as the two phone numbers before that are?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know really who made this telephone book. It was omitted. I didn't make this.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd offer 65 ter 5923b into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will receive number P7396.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7396 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, sorry. Ms. Stewart reminds that I didn't tender 65 ter 21062b. This was the intercept dated 17 July at 2340 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document receives number P7397.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7397 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I'd ask that that be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is admitted under seal. Witness, you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remembered for the OTP the names of the commanding officers and the soldier that I couldn't recall previously. If they still need it, I can tell them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. If Ms. Hasan would like to hear them, then she'll ask you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So do you remember the name of the --

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man called Lepir, his first name is Dragan, at Veliki Zep. And the soldiers who were with me, I remember two name: Ljubisa Sucur and Predrag Cinco. I remembered two names but many more of them rotated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If we can bring back P7396, page 3 in the English, page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I want to make absolutely clear that we under stood your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Page 3 in the -- in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Under the heading for "Commander," the two numbers that are listed as Belgrade as protected lines, where are those phone numbers physically located when General Mladic receives a call on them?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were staying at Vila Javor in the office where the ADC of General Mladic, Rajko Banduka, was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, earlier in the day at temporary transcript page 35, you were asked about the telephone available to General Mladic at the Vila Javor. By what means would calls by that phone at Vila Javor be transmitted when General Mladic wanted to talk to a commander of -- of the Drina Corps or one of the other corps of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically with the Drina Corps, if that's what he wanted to talk to, General Mladic would lift his receiver at this 064 number, and there was a number 332 at the switchboard there, and he would call the 332 number and ask to be connected to the commander of the Drina Corps or whoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would this line be protected or encrypted?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Protected, of course. KZU-71 was connected to it. The radio device FM-200 was working in the protected mode.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In your experience, would civilian PTT numbers ever be used by General Mladic to convey orders to the commander of the Drina Corps or any other subordinate corps commander?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic exclusively communicated with his subordinate units, specifically the corps commanders and the Presidency, on secure lines. He had direct channels, his own channels, with all the commanders, with the Presidency, and with the chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could now turn to P1655 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And not broadcast the same, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you have heard at temporary transcript page 57, lines 8 through 11, that the Prosecution and the Defence agree that General Mladic is in Belgrade on this date and this time. Now if General Mladic is in Belgrade and if his words spoken in Belgrade were transmitted towards Crna Rijeka by a radio relay device, what route would be used?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The RRU device FM-200 was working on the Cer-Avala route on the 019 number. That was a digital protected route.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now we see from this document the Bosnian authorities who claim to be intercepting this conversation say that General Mladic is inaudible. They cannot hear him but they can hear the person talking in Crna Rijeka. Now, if General Mladic is in Belgrade and his words are being communicated towards Crna Rijeka via a radio relay device, what does this tell you about where this intercept would have to be located in order to hear the Crna Rijeka side of the conversation but not the General Mladic side of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If General Mladic was talking to Crna Rijeka, it was a protected route which you practically couldn't listen in on. Now I see that Pale is written here. I really don't know how.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But let's assume for the moment that someone can intercept but they can't hear the channel General Mladic is transmitting on. Based upon your knowledge of how radio relay devices work, what does that tell you about where that person intercepting would have to be physically located in relation to the radio relay device where General Mladic is transmitting from?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This conversation, in order to be intercepted, had to be either between these two stations at a particular radio relay route or very close, the stations, behind them. Otherwise, if the person was behind, that is, close to only one of these stations, these locations, then the intercepter would hear only one side of the conversation. But, again, in all cases, he would have to be very near.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And here the intercepter claims that they can only hear Crna Rijeka; they cannot hear General Mladic. So on which side would they have to be located? In whose territory?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the other side, on the Serbian side, if he is hearing Crna Rijeka. And if he is hearing General Mladic, he would be on our territory. In this case, if he's hearing Crna Rijeka and General Mladic is in Belgrade, the intercepter would have to be behind the radio relay device at Cer on the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you were asked about the RRU-800 from Cer to Veliki Zep. Was that ever used in the course of 1995? Was it ever placed into operative use?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That device, if I remember well, had been prepared and was used in September once when the Veliki Zep hub was bombed, but it was only for a couple of hours until we changed the antenna. We needed only a couple of hours to change the parabolic antenna system. It was sometime in September. I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And apart from that instance, was it ever utilized in 1995, in the time-period prior to September 1995?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was never any need because SMC was working well. There were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in -- in talking about the SMC you said that although analogue it was protected, and you mentioned the antennae that were used for that device. Could you describe for us the antenna that were used to both transmit and receive radio relay transmissions going through the SMC-1306B?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It used a round parabolic antenna with a diameter of 1.8 to 2.5 metres, depending on the distance. From the antenna of the device, a wave carrier was installed between the antenna and the device. So it was a very large parabolic antenna, up to 2.5 metres in diameter, and it was set on a concrete pedestal, and it was connected to the device not with cables but with a wave transmission device.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pajic, I thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is all I had in re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one short question. You were asked quite a number of questions by Mr. Ivetic about this communication between Belgrade and Crna Rijeka; that is, if the most simple option of communication would have been used, whereas there were other options as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The question of the Bench has not triggered any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Irrespective of the options that could be used to communicate between Belgrade and Crna Rijeka, if it is being transmitted by a radio relay device, does that change your answer as to where a party would have to be physically located to hear Crna Rijeka and not hear General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Irrespective of the options that could be used by General Mladic to communicate between Belgrade and Crna Rijeka, if that communication is being transmitted by a radio relay device, would any of those options change your answer as to where a party would have to be physically located to intercept that radio relay communication and hear only the channel with Crna Rijeka and not hear the channel with General Mladic's voice?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pajic, this concludes your testimony in this court, assuming that Ms. Hasan has no further questions. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered, sometimes in many technical details, the questions that were put to you by the parties and that were put to you by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you for your co-operation and understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and will resume -- yes, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: A quick point of clarification. It relates to the objection I made during Mr. Ivetic's direct examination. If we could briefly go into private session. It will just take a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not yet in private session. Always wait until I've thanked Madam Registrar. I've now thanked you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 21st of May, same courtroom, I, 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of May, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
